name: Firefox resistFingerprinting (privacy.resistFingerprinting, 'RFP') and letterboxing (privacy.resistFingerprinting.letterboxing); plus its successor surface privacy.fingerprintingProtection ('FPP') with RFPTargets and privacy.fingerprintingProtection.granularOverrides
kind: Browser feature (a set of about:config preferences in Gecko), upstreamed from Tor Browser under the Tor Uplift project. Not a standard, not an extractor.
maturity: Production but bifurcating. RFP is production and stable-but-frozen in posture; FPP with per-target RFPTargets is the actively developed path and is what Mozilla now surfaces to ordinary users via Enhanced Tracking Protection's Fingerprinting Protection mode. Downstream forks (LibreWolf) have publicly debated moving their default from RFP to FPP. Treat RFP as legacy-strong and FPP as the moving target.
license: MPL 2.0. Permits use in this project without restriction. Enabling a preference carries no licensing implication at all.
keeps_and_discards: Not an extraction approach; it discards nothing from the document. It discards environment entropy: screen and window dimensions are quantised (letterboxing rounds the content viewport to a step and pads with margins), timezone is reported as UTC, locale is forced toward en-US, canvas readback is blocked behind a per-site permission prompt, font enumeration is restricted to a system allowlist, WebGL and media-device enumeration are narrowed, prefers-color-scheme and prefers-reduced-motion are pinned, and high-resolution timers are coarsened. Under FPP the same list becomes a la carte via RFPTargets, so 'what is discarded' is a per-profile configuration rather than a fixed set — which is the important operational difference from Tor Browser.
structure_preserved: Completely. RFP/FPP never touch the DOM: nesting, ordering, tabular relations and shadow boundaries are exactly upstream Firefox's. Open shadow roots traverse; closed roots do not; declarative shadow DOM parses normally. Unlike Tor Browser there is no security-slider equivalent that disables JavaScript, so script-built structure is always present. Letterboxing changes the visual viewport only, which propagates to computed layout and media queries but not to the tree.
interactive_elements: Untouched. Controls remain ordinary DOM nodes with their handlers intact, because scripts always run. The one interaction-relevant change is the canvas permission prompt, which can block a script mid-flow and leave a page in a partially initialised state if the automation does not answer it.
interactive_state_fidelity: Fully preserved and, unlike Tor Browser's Safest level, preserved honestly: because JavaScript always executes, disabled / checked / selected / aria-expanded / aria-checked reflect real post-script state rather than initial-parse state. The accessibility tree is unaffected. RFP therefore costs zero tokens and zero state fidelity in the extraction sense; every cost it imposes lands in geometry and environment, which is precisely the half this project already exiles to the peripheral. That is the strongest single argument for RFP over heavier hardening here.
layout_awareness: Layout-perturbing, not layout-reading, and this is where it bites. Letterboxing quantises innerWidth/innerHeight and inserts margins, so getBoundingClientRect, IntersectionObserver thresholds, scroll extents, media-query breakpoints and any responsive-layout branch all shift. Font-allowlist restriction additionally changes text metrics and line-breaking. Everything RFP does that matters to this project happens downstream of the fold and inside the geometry peripheral.
javascript_required: Scripts always run — RFP has no JS-off mode. Telemetry therefore fires on every capture exactly as it would unhardened, which is the honest position: RFP reduces what telemetry can learn, it does not reduce whether telemetry fires. That is the opposite trade from tracker blocking, which suppresses the requests and pays a measured fidelity cost for it.
evaluation_method: Mozilla evaluates by target enumeration and web-compat regression triage rather than by benchmark: each RFPTarget is argued to remove a specific entropy source, and breakage is caught through Bugzilla and the webcompat pipeline. External evaluation is entropy measurement (EFF Cover Your Tracks, AmIUnique) and academic fingerprinting surveys. There is no extraction-fidelity evaluation of RFP anywhere, by anyone.
corpus_size_and_origins: No fixed corpus for either entropy or breakage. Web-compat evidence is user-reported bugs, which is an unbounded and heavily biased sample toward sites people actually complained about. The independent entropy instruments run on self-selected privacy-interested volunteers. Nothing here is a frozen page set, so no number quoted about RFP has a stable denominator.
reported_precision_recall: Not applicable; there is no precision/recall notion. The nearest published quantity is fingerprint-uniqueness reduction, which is reported qualitatively by Mozilla and by bucket by Cover Your Tracks rather than as a rate. [uncertain] No current measurement of residual entropy under FPP-with-default-RFPTargets at a stated Firefox version was located.
independent_oracle: Yes, partially: EFF Cover Your Tracks and AmIUnique are operated independently of Mozilla and do not share its implementation assumptions. They are weak oracles in two ways — self-selected populations, and they can only test vectors they already know. For this project a much better oracle is available locally and does not exist in the literature: run the same page through the same fold with RFP on and off and diff the trie. That is an oracle-free fidelity test in the project's own terms, and it is cheap.
evidence_independence: Design and target rationale are first-party Mozilla. Entropy measurement is third-party. Breakage evidence is crowd-sourced and unsystematic. No vendor-run fidelity comparison exists because no vendor sells RFP.
page_archetype_coverage: No published per-archetype figures. Structurally, RFP should be close to archetype-neutral for text content because it never removes DOM, and archetype-sensitive only for pages whose content depends on a responsive breakpoint or on canvas-rendered output. Product and collection pages with breakpoint-switched markup, and documentation sites that render diagrams to canvas, are the two categories where RFP could plausibly change what is captured. Article, forum and service pages should be unaffected in content terms. This is a mechanism-derived prediction, not a measurement. [uncertain]
script_and_locale_behaviour: The locale forcing is the sharpest edge. RFP reports en-US and UTC regardless of the real profile, so sites that branch server- or client-side on Accept-Language or on Intl output will serve a different-language document than an unhardened capture of the same URL. That is a content change, not a geometry change, and it would show up as fold drift attributable entirely to hardening. Font-allowlist restriction also degrades CJK and Indic shaping and changes line-breaking, which perturbs geometry but not text. For a whitespace-free-segmentation script the text is unchanged; for a multilingual corpus the served document may not be. This deserves explicit measurement before RFP is enabled on any live-site arm.
leaks_outward: Reduces what a page can learn about the machine — screen, timezone, locale, fonts, canvas, media devices, timer resolution — without reducing what it learns about the visit. Network-level disclosure is entirely unchanged: same IP, same TLS fingerprint, same request volume. Against the local measurement of roughly 3,082 external requests to 92+ hosts per corpus run, RFP changes nothing; every one of those requests still fires, merely carrying less entropy.
mechanism_detectability: Detectable, cheaply, and actively used in production. RFP is a positive tell rather than an absence: a profile reporting UTC timezone with en-US locale and a screen size that is an exact letterbox multiple, alongside coarsened performance.now(), is a recognisable and commonly-checked combination. Commercial fingerprinting SDKs (FingerprintJS and its lineage, plus the anti-bot vendors) explicitly enumerate RFP-consistent attribute sets, and mismatch checks — a UTC timezone against a non-UTC IP geolocation, an en-US locale against a European exit — are standard scoring inputs at DataDome, Cloudflare and Akamai today. Critically for this project's stated tension, RFP does NOT set or unset navigator.webdriver and does nothing to hide Marionette: it is orthogonal to automation detection. Enabling RFP alongside geckodriver produces a session that is both flagged as automated (navigator.webdriver true) and flagged as hardened (RFP attribute set) — two independent tells rather than one masking the other.
countermeasures: FPP with granularOverrides is the real countermeasure to RFP's own conspicuousness: per-target, per-domain enabling lets the operator keep the targets that matter (canvas, fonts) and drop the ones that generate the loudest mismatch (timezone, locale). privacy.resistFingerprinting.letterboxing can be toggled independently of RFP, which is the single most useful knob here — it removes the viewport quantisation while keeping the rest, and viewport quantisation is the part that disturbs the geometry peripheral.
measured_fidelity_cost: Not published anywhere, and directly measurable locally at low cost. The relevant local anchors: the null control establishes a 0.07% fold-drift floor, so any RFP arm below roughly 0.1% is indistinguishable from noise; block_trackers costs 10.49% on live sites versus 0.16% on saved pages, which sets the scale of a hardening arm that suppresses requests. RFP suppresses no requests, so the a priori expectation is that RFP-minus-locale-forcing lands near the null floor on live sites, and that RFP-with-locale-forcing lands materially above it on any multilingual or geo-branching site. That split — locale forcing as the dominant cost term — is the specific hypothesis worth testing. [uncertain]
gate_state_at_capture: RFP records nothing about gate state and does not change gate incidence much, because the IP is unchanged and IP reputation dominates challenge decisions. The second-order effect runs through the mismatch signals above: a UTC/en-US profile on a European residential IP raises anti-bot risk scores at some vendors and can therefore increase CAPTCHA incidence relative to an unhardened control. With roughly 67% of top sites already presenting a consent interface, gate state must be recorded per capture regardless; RFP neither helps nor hinders that.
determinism: Improves run-to-run determinism of everything environment-derived, which is a genuine and under-appreciated benefit for this project. Pinned timezone, locale, colour scheme, reduced-motion and quantised viewport all remove sources of capture-to-capture variance that would otherwise present as spurious fold drift. Content determinism is unchanged.
determinism_across_versions: Poor, and worse than Tor Browser's because the surface is being actively refactored. The RFPTargets set, its defaults, and the letterbox step have all changed across Firefox releases, and Mozilla's public direction is toward FPP defaults, which will change them again. Any measured fidelity cost is valid only for a pinned Firefox version, and the pin must be recorded with the measurement.
reproducibility: Reproducible if and only if the Firefox version, the exact preference set (RFP vs FPP, letterboxing on/off, granularOverrides string), and the page itself are all pinned. The preference set in particular is easy to under-record — 'RFP on' is not a sufficient description once FPP and granular overrides exist. Given that 75% of the local corpus pages fetch live resources on every read, the corpus is the weaker link, not RFP.
failure_modes: Canvas permission prompts stalling scripted flows; sites serving a different language because of forced locale; responsive-breakpoint content differences caused by letterbox quantisation; broken canvas-rendered charts and diagrams; occasional hard breakage on sites that use canvas for layout measurement; and elevated anti-bot risk scores from geo/timezone mismatch.
failure_visibility: Mostly silent, which is the principal argument for measuring rather than assuming. A locale-switched page is a well-formed, plausible, wrong capture. A breakpoint-switched layout is a well-formed, plausible, differently-populated capture. Neither raises an error. Only the canvas prompt and hard breakage are loud. This is the exact silent-degradation class the project refuses, so RFP should be treated as requiring a measured arm before it is enabled anywhere in a measured path.
scale_limits: None of consequence. RFP costs no throughput and no memory; it is preference evaluation inside Gecko. Cost remains linear in pages.
delta_cost_model: No delta model of its own, and one specific interaction worth naming: because letterboxing quantises the viewport, a window-size change smaller than the letterbox step produces no geometry change at all, while a change that crosses a step boundary produces a whole-page geometry change with zero DOM mutation. That is a change entirely outside a mutation-driven delta model — no MutationObserver record fires, yet every cached rect is stale. If the geometry peripheral is ever cached, letterboxing must be an explicit invalidation trigger.
reanchoring_stability: Neutral for DOM-keyed anchors: xpath, content hash and CDC boundaries are unaffected because the DOM is unaffected. Negative for any anchor that incorporates geometry or viewport-visibility, which letterboxing quantises and version-drifts. This is an argument for keeping node identity strictly DOM-derived — which the trie key already does.
adversarial_exposure: No help whatsoever. RFP preserves zero-width characters, Unicode tag characters, HTML comments, JSON-LD and every off-screen or display:none node exactly as authored, and has no concept of concealment. There is one adverse interaction: letterboxing changes the viewport, and viewport-based hiding is 1,802 of the concealed injections in the 2026 in-the-wild census — so a letterboxed capture's notion of 'outside the visible area' differs from an unhardened one's. Any concealment filter that ever did read geometry would produce different answers under RFP than without it, which is another reason to keep concealment filtering off the geometry axis.
provenance_carrying: None at the representation level. It does contribute one fact that belongs in the capture envelope: the exact hardening configuration (RFP/FPP, letterboxing state, granularOverrides, Firefox version), without which a fidelity number is uninterpretable.
roundtrip_safety: Not applicable; no serialisation step, no escaping policy, no text normalisation.
token_budget_and_ordering: No effect. RFP imposes no truncation, no reordering, and no context policy.
representation_cost: Zero token delta in the normal case, because the DOM is unchanged. Non-zero only where forced locale causes a differently-sized document to be served, or where a breakpoint change alters how much markup the page emits.
what_could_be_adopted: Adoptable as-is, with one part carved out. The recommended configuration for this project is FPP with granularOverrides rather than blanket RFP, letterboxing explicitly OFF, and locale/timezone forcing explicitly OFF — keeping canvas, font-enumeration, media-device and timer-resolution targets. That combination removes the entropy sources that cost nothing (they touch no DOM and no served document) while dropping the two that do cost — viewport quantisation, which disturbs the geometry peripheral and creates a delta-model blind spot, and locale forcing, which can change the served document outright. The second adoptable idea is structural rather than technical: RFP demonstrates that the cheapest hardening is hardening that never touches the document, and it gives this project a clean way to separate hardening cost into 'document-affecting' and 'environment-affecting' arms.

constraint_violation_ledger.verdict: Adoptable as-is in the reduced configuration (FPP, letterboxing off, locale forcing off); the letterboxing and locale-forcing components are adoptable in the actuator layer only, and letterboxing is arguably rejected outright given the delta blind spot it creates.
constraint_violation_ledger.structure_agnosticism: No conflict. RFP applies no structural heuristic, names no region, and touches no tag or interactivity signal. Fully compatible.
constraint_violation_ledger.no_layout_in_the_fold: Compatible only with letterboxing disabled. With letterboxing on, viewport quantisation perturbs the geometry peripheral in a version-dependent way. It never puts layout in the fold, so this is an actuator-layer concern, not a fold violation.
constraint_violation_ledger.o_delta: One concrete violation to guard: a letterbox step crossing changes all geometry with zero mutation records, which is a change outside any mutation-driven delta model. With letterboxing off, RFP is delta-neutral.
constraint_violation_ledger.no_mocks: Fully compatible. RFP runs in a real browser, runs all page scripts, and stubs nothing. It is strictly better than Tor Browser's Safest level on this axis, which is the single strongest reason to prefer RFP over Tor Browser here.
constraint_violation_ledger.closed_shadow_roots_stay_closed: Fully consistent. RFP provides no shadow-root access of any kind and no attachShadow interference. Closed roots stay closed.

governance_signal_handling: None. RFP sends no bot-identifying signal, reads no robots.txt, and has no AIPREF, Content Signals, ai.txt, Web Bot Auth or HTTP 402 awareness. It is orthogonal to the governance layer: it changes what the site learns about the machine, not whether the site has consented to the visit. Note that it is compatible with Web Bot Auth in a way Tor is not — signing a request with a stable agent key and hardening the browser fingerprint are independent, and doing both is coherent (declare identity at the protocol layer, withhold entropy at the API layer).
legal_basis_and_pii_posture: Under EDPB Guidelines 03/2026 the regulated act is the collection and persistent storage of personal data from public sources; the browser's fingerprint posture does not bear on the lawful basis for that storage. RFP does have one modest defensive value in the legitimate-interest balancing: reducing the entropy disclosed to third parties during capture limits the controller's own contribution to tracking of the operator, which is a data-minimisation argument about the capture process rather than about the artifact. It retains no PII and adds none.
